clue.text: Initial drudgery in the garden

parts.note: the hard groundwork done before any project, pictured literally as digging over a garden bed with a spade

explanation.surface: Digging over the plot is the first chore of the gardening year.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundwork or preparatory toil is figuratively the digging done before planting.

clue.text: Head for the food

definitions.meaning: the top or crown of the head, an old word for the skull
a savoury paste of meat or fish spread on toast, written with accents in French

explanation.surface: A chef asks which part of the animal goes into the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves both the crown of the skull and the French meat spread.

clue.text: Cause a collapse in the river level

indicators.note: the level is placed in the river, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
flat means level, even

explanation.surface: Flooding risk as the water level of a river changes.
explanation.walkthrough: The level is placed in the river, splitting it after its second letter; 'in' is the container signal, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To let the air out of a tyre or balloon makes it collapse.

clue.text: Nothing we hope spoils the fun

indicators.note: spoils suggests damaging and disordering, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A party-goer hopes nothing will ruin the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of exuberant joy, used as a noun for boisterous merrymaking and revelry.

clue.text: Set up a European capital

parts.note: to rig is to set up or fit out, as with a ship's sails or equipment

explanation.surface: A capital city is founded somewhere in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latvian seat of government on the Baltic.

clue.text: Pervading atmosphere that's quite agreeable…

parts.note: an atmosphere is a mood in a room, and one suggesting that people are pleased with something is described

explanation.surface: A room fills with a pleasant, contented mood, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the next clue down; each is a cryptic definition of a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A look or manner suggesting that someone likes and endorses something.

clue.text: … with such attractiveness on the distaff side

definitions.text: with such attractiveness on the distaff side

parts.words: with such attractiveness on the distaff side
parts.note: the distaff side is the women of a family, so this is the appeal of a woman

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the pleasant mood comes from the ladies' allure.
explanation.walkthrough: The distaff, a spindle for spinning wool, was a symbol of women's work, so 'the distaff side' means the female side.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure or grace traditionally attributed to women.

clue.text: Free food parcel, so to speak, for the Apostles?

definitions.text: Free food parcel, so to speak, for the Apostles?

parts.words: Free food parcel, so to speak, for the Apostles?
parts.note: a free present of ox tongues as food is one reading; the other is the Pentecost power of speaking in other languages

explanation.surface: A charity hamper delivered to twelve disciples.
explanation.walkthrough: At Pentecost (Acts 2) the Apostles were able to speak in languages they had never learnt.
explanation.definitionFit: The miraculous ability to speak unknown languages, bestowed on the Apostles.

clue.text: Company rate not for bargaining

definitions.note: the definition describes the noun phrase as a fixed sum offered with no haggling

parts.note: a firm is a business company
a price is a rate charged

explanation.surface: A business sets a charge that cannot be negotiated.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition overlaps the wordplay loosely: 'rate not for bargaining' describes the whole phrase too.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed cost that the seller will not reduce through haggling.

clue.text: Unhealthy bunch in which an OT character is spotted

definitions.text: Unhealthy bunch in which an OT character is spotted

parts.words: Unhealthy bunch in which an OT character is spotted
parts.note: a poor lot that also suggests Lot, the Old Testament figure, covered in measles spots

explanation.surface: A sickly crowd in which a figure from the Old Testament is recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: Lot is Abraham's nephew in Genesis; measles gives spots, and 'measly' means paltry.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserable, paltry group or collection.

clue.text: Press club

definitions.meaning: to smooth clothes with a heated appliance
a golf club with an angled metal head

explanation.surface: A reporters' society, as in a press club.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers smoothing laundry and a metal-headed golf stick.

clue.text: Time to map out a Florida holiday resort

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: It is time to plan a trip to a Florida resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of 'map' to sit between the abbreviation for time and the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A city on Florida's Gulf coast, popular with tourists.

clue.text: Small number at the Council of Europe develop a bad habit

parts.note: six in Roman numerals is VI, a small number
CE is the abbreviation for the Council of Europe

explanation.surface: A minor delegate at a European body falls into wicked ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral failing or an ingrained wicked practice.

clue.text: Six against one, note, striking

parts.note: six in Roman numerals is VI
V is short for versus, against
one is the Roman numeral I
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: An unfair fight of six against one makes a dramatic scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright and vibrant, making a strong impression.

clue.text: Kind of information to get about

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone tries to find out about something.
explanation.definitionFit: A category or sort, especially of art or literature.

clue.text: One of Ruth's people giving the doctor something to eat

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
a bite, a snack, is something to eat

explanation.surface: A biblical figure feeds a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth, of the Old Testament book named after her, came from the land of Moab.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Moab, Ruth's homeland in the Bible.

clue.text: Featured open-and-shut cases

parts.note: featured means part of the face, and the coverings that open and close over the eyes are cases

explanation.surface: Simple, obvious legal cases were in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: The folds of skin that cover and protect each eye.

clue.text: Duplicated copy

parts.note: a copy made as a duplicate of an original artwork or object

explanation.definitionFit: An exact reproduction of something.

clue.text: Unbelievable doctrine of wan hamite

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Unbelievable doctrine of wan hamite (7)': the anagram needs HAMITES (an S missing) and 'wan' fits nothing; the printed text cannot be recovered.

clue.text: Punishable crime at a pinch

parts.note: to pinch is to steal, so the crime is committed whenever something is pinched

explanation.surface: In an emergency, something criminal might be committed.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal term for theft.

clue.text: Cross greyhound on the prowl

definitions.meaning: a cross-bred dog with greyhound blood, used by poachers
one who lurks or prowls about, an old sense

explanation.surface: An angry racing dog goes hunting.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbreed hunting dog, and also an old word for a prowler or petty thief.

clue.text: Bird with a dovelike sound on the square

parts.note: the soft murmur of a dove is a coo
a T-square is a drawing tool, so the square gives T

explanation.surface: A bird coos in the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A black water bird with a white forehead shield.

clue.text: Hears out part

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone listens to one section of the hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion or allotted fraction.

clue.text: Ducks a greeting in a Ryder Cup setting

indicators.note: the greeting is placed in the ducks, inside them

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so two ducks are two Os
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A golfer waves hello while dodging at a golf tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1987 Ryder Cup, the golf match between Europe and the USA, was played at Muirfield Village in this state.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state that hosted the golf tournament in 1987.

clue.text: Commercials we hear for a cutting tool

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: ads are advertisements

explanation.surface: Adverts on the radio promote a sharp tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An axe-like tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle, used for shaping wood.

clue.text: Those having no time may put their foot in it

definitions.text: may put their foot in it

indicators.note: having no time means the letter for time is removed

explanation.surface: People in a rush are liable to blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put their foot in it' usually means make a gaffe; here people literally put feet into stockings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockings or tights, garments worn on the legs and feet.

clue.text: Advertisement carried for a square meal?

definitions.text: Advertisement carried for a square meal?

parts.words: Advertisement carried for a square meal?
parts.note: a pair of placards worn front and back by a person, hinting at a meal between slices of bread

explanation.surface: A poster carried by someone who works in exchange for a hearty dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of advertising boards hung over the shoulders, front and back.

clue.text: Appropriate place for starting stalls

parts.note: a fresh trading site where stalls might open, and a famous racecourse with starting stalls for horses

explanation.surface: A suitable spot to open market stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: Newmarket in Suffolk is the home of British horse racing; starting stalls are the gates horses start from.
explanation.definitionFit: A Suffolk town famous for racing, where horses leave the stalls.
